analysis.title: Tesla, Inc. Takeout helps, but we're also seeing improved trajectory in core biz + Robotaxi - upgrade to OW
key_insights: Barclays upgrades TSLA to Overweight from Equal Weight and raises its price target to $450 from $370 (+20.9% vs $372.22 close on 23-Oct-26). The call rests on M&A optionality, a stronger core business outlook and early Robotaxi inflection.

A TSLA/SPCX merger is viewed as likely. On the SPCX earnings call Musk said special committees had formed at both companies and that there was 'a lot of merit to combining the companies.' Barclays expects a premium to the TSLA price at announcement and sees downside limited because investors will be hesitant to short ahead of a possible deal.

Timing: it was reported that Musk wants to announce a merger by 1H27 so it closes under the current administration. Barclays calls this reasonable. An announcement could come in the coming months ahead of Tesla's AGM (Dec 3), or at some point in 1H27.

Rationale: the merger would likely be pitched as AI vertical integration (superintelligence software, chip design, Terafab, robotics). Barclays sees Musk's wish to consolidate control as the key driver. He wants ~25% of Tesla versus ~20% now. He owns ~48% of SpaceX and has ~82% of SPCX voting power through Class B shares.

Valuation: a ~$450 TSLA price implies a ~20% premium to ~$372. With SPCX at ~$147 (~$2.0tn market cap) and TSLA at ~$450 (~$1.8tn), SPCX would offer ~3.1x its shares per TSLA share. On those values Musk would hold ~53% of combined voting power. Barclays expects an all-stock deal with SPCX as acquirer, not a debt-financed one.

Shareholder approval is not assured. More than 50% of total outstanding TSLA voting power must approve, and abstentions count as 'No'. Past votes show the gap: Musk's 2025 pay package got 77% of cast votes but 68% of outstanding votes, and the xAI investment got 54% of cast votes but only 38% of outstanding, so it failed. Even with Musk's ~20% voting yes, ~35-40% of the remaining shares would need to approve. Whether Musk recuses himself is an open question, and Texas law does not require it.

Auto volumes are returning to growth after two years of decline. Barclays estimates 1.80mn units for 2026 (from ~1.65mn), 1.92mn for 2027 (from ~1.82mn) and 2.09mn for 2028 (from ~1.98mn), modestly above consensus. Tesla ended 3Q with its largest passenger-vehicle backlog in four years and added ~175k units of reported capacity YTD. Barclays' 2026 auto margin estimate is 17.6%, up ~230bps y/y.

FSD is a demand and margin driver. Active FSD subscriptions are up ~60% y/y YTD. FSD penetration on North American deliveries was over 75% in 3Q, up ~20pts q/q. FSD revenue flows through at near 100% margin. A forthcoming European regulatory vote on FSD could add volume there.

China exports from Giga Shanghai are now ~25-30% of Tesla's global volumes, with record deliveries in markets such as Australia and Japan in 3Q. Barclays assumes they are margin-accretive because of the APAC regional mix. Musk set a 2030 target of 5mn units against consensus of 2.7mn and Barclays' 2.6mn.

Energy is nearly sold out of Megapacks for 2027 on 'extreme demand' from data centers. With the Houston Megafactory (~50 GWh planned) starting in 4Q, Barclays sees at least 50% y/y growth in 2027 energy deployments. Management guided Energy ASPs and margins to improve, reversing earlier talk of margin compression from Chinese competition, policy and cell tariffs.
Out-year revenue revisions have stabilized and are up slightly from the 2Q trough, after several years of declines.

Robotaxi is showing early inflection. As of Oct 18 it had driven ~3.1mn unsupervised miles across 6 cities (Austin 2.1mn, Dallas 0.6mn, Houston 0.2mn), against ~0.4mn at 2Q earnings in mid-July. Weekly miles rose from ~70k in mid-July to ~560k in the week of Oct 12-19, with ~20% average w/w growth.

Austin Robotaxi miles reached ~438k in the latest week, more than 5x the pre-Cybercab peak of ~83k. Weekly miles have grown at a 27% CAGR in the 7 weeks since the early-September Cybercab launch, alongside a 10x increase in the Cybercab fleet. Barclays does not expect Robotaxi to be financially material near to mid term, but says progress could drive the stock narrative, and Austin market-share data could be a catalyst.

The $450 PT comes from a 2030 probability-weighted scenario analysis with a 4% discount rate over 4 years and a 95x base-case EPS multiple (prior 85x). It is driven mostly by the expected merger premium. $420 (a 13% premium) would be a low-end symbolic number, and Brad Gerstner of Altimeter cited $420-550. Bloomberg consensus SPCX PT is $247 and Barclays' SPCX PT is $300.

Upside case is $550 (a larger premium and/or SPCX outperformance). Downside case is $250, mainly a deal that never materializes, fails a shareholder vote or hits regulatory problems. Barclays notes a failed vote could leave Musk less engaged at Tesla.

Technical factors support the stock. The 'Tesla-financial complex' of heavy options activity can drive gamma squeezes. Average notional options trading is ~$80bn, versus ~$100bn average and ~$245bn on Nov 8 after the 2024 election. The call-to-put ratio is ~1.5x. Retail holds an estimated ~40% of shares outstanding.

Barclays' estimates: 2026E EPS $1.64 (consensus $1.73), 2027E EPS $1.28 (consensus $2.20) and 2028E EPS $1.55. Free cash flow is $527mn in 2026E and negative in 2027E (-$6.1bn) and 2028E (-$4.3bn) as capex rises to $19.8bn, $24.2bn and $28.1bn.

market_movers.rationale: Upgraded from Equal Weight on expected SPCX merger premium, improving auto and energy outlook and early Robotaxi inflection. PT raised 22% from $370, with upside case $550 and downside case $250.

sector_views.rationale: Barclays keeps its industry view at Neutral, unchanged, while upgrading TSLA within the coverage universe.

earnings_insights: TSLA 3Q26 EPS reported $0.48 (adjusted, Barclays table 'A' actual), versus $0.50 in 3Q25 (-4% y/y) and Bloomberg consensus of $0.62 as shown in the consensus column.

Barclays quarterly EPS (adjusted): 1Q26 $0.41 actual, 2Q26 $0.33 actual, 3Q26 $0.48 actual, 4Q26 $0.42 estimate (Bloomberg consensus $0.46 est). FY26 EPS estimate is $1.64 (consensus est $1.73) against 2025 actual $1.66.
Barclays FY27 EPS estimate is $1.28 (-22% y/y), versus Bloomberg consensus est of $2.20. Barclays FY28 EPS estimate is $1.55.
Barclays 2026E revenue is $107,990mn versus $94,827mn in 2025A. 2027E revenue is $115,442mn and 2028E is $127,836mn. Adjusted EBITDA is $14,027mn for 2026E and adjusted EBIT is $6,993mn.
On the 3Q earnings call management said the Energy business is almost sold out of Megapacks for 2027 and guided Energy ASPs and margins to improve.
Management noted FSD penetration over 75% on North American deliveries in 3Q and that Robotaxi weekly miles are growing at double-digit w/w rates.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight TSLA with $450 12-month price target, upgraded from Equal Weight
trade_ideas.rationale: Expected SPCX merger premium plus improved core auto and energy trajectory and Robotaxi inflection offer attractive risk/reward.
trade_ideas.risk: Deal fails to materialize, is rejected by shareholders or regulators, or core demand weakens and competition forces price cuts.

risk_factors: Merger risk: the deal may never be announced, may fail the TSLA shareholder vote (more than 50% of outstanding voting power needed, abstentions count against), or may hit regulatory challenges.
Without M&A, the stock loses a support Barclays believes it currently has, and concerns about the business outlook could re-emerge.
Demand weakening that pressures auto volume growth and forces larger price cuts.
Slower progress on AI initiatives including FSD, Robotaxi and Optimus.
Increased competition from legacy OEM and new-entrant EVs causing share loss or price cuts.
A failed shareholder vote could make Musk less engaged at Tesla.
Capex rising to $19.8bn in 2026E and $24.2bn in 2027E drives negative free cash flow in 2027E and 2028E.
charts_described: Figure 1 shows Elon Musk's hypothetical post-merger combined company ownership, with ~53% voting power on $2.0tn/$1.8tn valuations.

Figure 2 shows annual TSLA deliveries by model, with total deliveries of 1,809k (2023), 1,789k (2024), 1,636k (2025), 1,853k (2026E), 1,944k (2027E), 2,079k (2028E), 2,334k (2029E) and 2,613k (2030E).
Figure 6 shows cumulative Robotaxi miles rising to 3.1mn by October 2026, and Figure 7 shows weekly Robotaxi miles rising from 89k (week of 8/3) to 558k (week of 10/12).
vol_and_positioning: TSLA call-to-put ratio has been consistently elevated and was most recently ~1.5x.

Average notional TSLA options trading value is ~$80bn recently, versus a ~$100bn average from the 2024 election to mid-December 2024 and ~$245bn on Fri Nov 8, 2024 against $310bn for the rest of the market.
Barclays cites the FT's 'Tesla-financial complex' concept, where outsized options activity can skew the stock and drive gamma squeezes.
Retail investors are estimated to hold ~40% of TSLA shares outstanding.
Barclays says investors are likely to be hesitant to short TSLA ahead of a potential merger announcement, which limits downside.
geopolitical: Reported Musk goal of announcing a SpaceX/Tesla merger by 1H27 so it closes before the current US administration leaves office, given a more supportive M&A backdrop and Musk's relationship with the administration.
Chinese competition in energy storage and tariffs on battery cells cited as past margin headwinds, with the US seeing less Chinese competition than other regions.
cross_bank_references: Barclays colleague Anthony Valentini covers SPCX with a $300 PT, against a Bloomberg consensus PT of $247.

tension_points.bull_case: Barclays expects an all-stock SPCX acquisition of TSLA at a premium (~$420 to $500+, base ~$450). The premium supports the upside, and investors' reluctance to short ahead of a deal limits downside. Core auto, energy and Robotaxi trends add support.
tension_points.bear_case: Timing is uncertain and the deal needs more than 50% of total outstanding TSLA votes, with abstentions counting against. Past votes such as the xAI investment (38% of outstanding) failed that bar. A failed deal could leave Musk less engaged, and the stock would lose its M&A support.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A deal not being announced, or a failed TSLA shareholder vote or regulatory challenge. Barclays sets $250 as the downside case if the deal does not materialize.
